artifacts.title: Speck v. Missouri Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Ryan Speck complained that Missouri Presbytery erred in declining to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE Greg Johnson regarding four allegations arising from his involvement in and teaching at the Revoice 2018 conference; the SJC sustained the complaint in part on Issue 1 (particularly regarding Theological Judgments 2, 3, and 5 about terminology, gay identity, and spiritual friendship), denied Issues 2 and 3, and remanded the matter to Missouri Presbytery for a new hearing on specific questions.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Paul M. Wright filed a complaint against Eastern Carolina Presbytery regarding its response to a Reference from White Oak Presbyterian Church Session on a doctrinal issue. The SJC found the case judicially out of order because the Presbytery's action was advice only in response to a Reference for advice under BCO 41-1, and such advisory actions are not complainable under BCO 43. The Panel recommended the case be found out of order. Vote: 17 concurring, 1 dissenting (RE J. Howard Donahoe), 1 abstaining, 4 absent.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Andy Lee challenged Korean Capital Presbytery's suspension of the Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington Session and appointment of a commission to act for it without prior congregational consent. The SJC sustained both issues, holding the presbytery lacked authority for the intervention and annulling all subsequent acts of the commission acting as Session.

artifacts.title: CHARLES KIM v. KOREAN CAPITAL PRESBYTERY
artifacts.synopsis: TE Sung Keon Kim challenged Korean Capital Presbytery's suspension of the Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington Session and replacement of its functions by a presbytery commission without prior congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint, held that the presbytery lacked authority to take that action under the BCO and Preliminary Principle Six, and annulled the commission's subsequent acts.

artifacts.synopsis: TE David Bowen complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's actions rescinding its 1988 decision and annulling the elections and ordinations of ruling elders and deacons at the Church of the Good Shepherd who took exception to infant baptism and limited atonement. The SJC sustained the complaint that ECP erred in rescinding a two-year-old action and annulling ordinations without due process under BCO 24-6, while also affirming that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals of the system of doctrine for which no exceptions may be granted for church officers.

artifacts.title: Interpretation of 'papists' in WCF 24.3 for marriage eligibility

matches.evidence: The CCB declined Iowa Presbytery's reference asking whether 'papists' in WCF 24.3 means all Roman Catholics or only those holding Roman Catholic soteriology, finding no matter pending before the lower court.

artifacts.title: Declaring exceptions for non-literal six-day creationist views
artifacts.disposition: declined to take action — reference not proper; overture recommended for proper procedure

matches.evidence: The CCB declined to act, ruling that defining what constitutes an exception to the standards is beyond its scope; presbyteries wishing to set such a norm should overture the GA.

artifacts.title: Setting a nomination deadline before the one-month officer election notice
artifacts.disposition: advice given — session may set nomination deadline before one-month meeting notice; all six required elements must be included

matches.evidence: A session may set a nomination deadline before the one-month congregational meeting notice expires, but all six BCO 24-1 requirements for officer election must be met.
